Development stage

A shared dollar settlement network for cooperative finance

Dollar.coop is developing a cooperative network to help participating banks and financial institutions move and reuse prefunded digital dollars on the XRP Ledger. The design combines one dollar instrument with institutional controls, reconciliation and separately contracted redemption and local-currency payouts.

See how settlement worksExplore pilot design
Proposed settlement flow
1
FundAn eligible bank funds the issuer with final dollars.
2
TransferApproved banks transfer the same funded token on XRPL.
3
Reuse or redeemThe recipient can use its balance again or request fiat under the issuer’s terms.
Institutional use cases

Move and reuse funded balances

Eligible banks and cooperative financial institutions would choose whether to participate and retain responsibility for their customers, treasury and regulatory approvals. Federations can convene institutions and help define requirements. Each settlement participant needs its own approval.

Supplier settlement

Transfer a shared dollar claim between approved institutions and reconcile it against a reference held off ledger.

Treasury transfers

Reuse incoming token balances and see which funds are available or reserved.

Trade and payout corridors

Match dollar inflows to approved obligations. Local payouts depend on separate agreements and funding.

Optional design programme

Assess an institutional pilot

The proposed programme would document bank requirements, demonstrate synthetic settlement and assess one existing authorised issuer’s XRPL instrument. Institutional enquiries will open once contact routing and privacy terms are in place.

G4USD is a possible future issuer programme. It depends on verified issuer permissions, signed agreements and tested operating controls. Any cooperative service economics would require legal and tax review. The design offers no token-holder yield.

Sources checked 6 November 2026

US regulatory register

Agency rules cover specified entities and activities. Dollar.coop remains at the development stage. Any future instrument requires its own issuer and route approvals.

18 July 2025 · Enacted

GENIUS Act

The US statute establishes a framework for payment stablecoin issuers. The OCC identifies 18 January 2027 as the Act’s effective date.

Public Law 119-27

21 October 2026 · Final rule announced

OCC implementation

The OCC’s final rule for entities it supervises takes effect 18 January 2027. The OCC implementation page says application intake has yet to open.

Final rule
Application status

24 September 2026 · Two proposals

Federal Reserve

The proposals cover applications by Board-supervised banks for a subsidiary to issue stablecoins and substantive standards for Board-supervised issuers and other covered entities. Both comment periods close 30 November 2026.

Proposal notices

February and May 2026 · Proposals

NCUA

Licensing and operating proposals address the issuer pathway involving federally insured credit unions. Current NCUA guidance says federally chartered credit unions lack direct digital-asset custody authority.

Licensing proposal and custody guidance
Proposed issuer standards

17 August 2026 · Proposal

Treasury issuance and distribution

Treasury’s proposal addresses US issuance and distribution. Its notice distinguishes the 18 January 2027 framework date from the broader restriction on US offering or sale starting 18 July 2028.

Treasury proposal notice

30 September 2026 · Interim final rule

Treasury state certification

Procedures for reviewing state regulatory regimes took effect 30 September 2026. Comments close 30 November 2026. Certification of a regime is separate from an individual issuer’s permissions.

State certification rule

8 April 2026 · Joint proposal

FinCEN and OFAC

The proposal covers anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance programmes for permitted issuers.

Joint programme proposal

18 June 2026 · Joint proposal

Customer identification

FinCEN and the banking agencies proposed customer identification requirements for permitted issuers. The comment period closed 21 August 2026.

Customer identification docket
